content: 1. After at least five half-lives of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, adjust the dose of ivosidenib to the recommended 500 mg daily. Ivosidenib reduces the levels or effects of ritonavir by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for reduced therapeutic effects of these drugs. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Ritonavir and ixazomib interactions are minor, with no clinically significant changes in systemic exposure observed during trials with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Monitor closely. 4. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ketamine by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 6. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Monitor closely. 7. Ritonavir increases levels of lacosamide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Modify therapy and monitor closely to avoid potential toxicity. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 8. Ritonavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing its metabolism, potentially reducing lamotrigine levels by 50%. Adjust the lamotrigine dose as needed when starting, stopping, or changing ritonavir doses. Similar interactions may occur with other ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitors. 10. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Monitor closely. 11. Lapatinib increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3-5 half-lives. 13. Lasmiditan increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 15. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 16. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 17. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 18. Ritonavir increases levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir also increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. 19. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ritonavir increases levels of levocetirizine by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Levoketoconazole increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (intrauterine or oral) by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended. 24. Ritonavir increases levels of linagliptin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism but may decrease its effects due to insulin resistance. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 25. Ritonavir decreases liraglutide effects due to insulin resistance. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lofepramine by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lofexidine by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the lofexidine dose and monitor for orthostasis and bradycardia. 28. Ritonavir increases lomitapide levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Consider reducing the lomitapide dose if used concomitantly. 29. Ritonavir increases lonafarnib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to its sensitivity as a CYP3A4 substrate. 30. Ritonavir increases loperamide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Ritonavir increases lopinavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Ritonavir increases loratadine levels by altering CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism and inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Monitor closely. 33. Lorcaserin increases ritonavir levels by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Lorlatinib decreases ritonavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, while ritonavir increases lorlatinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day and adjust after discontinuing the CYP3A inhibitor. 35. Ritonavir increases losartan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Ritonavir increases lovastatin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 37. Ritonavir may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. Discontinue antiretrovirals at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 38. Ritonavir increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors. 39. Ritonavir increases lumateperone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Ritonavir may increase or decrease lumefantrine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Ritonavir increases lurasidone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 42. Ritonavir increases levels of lurbinectedin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50% if unavoidable. 43. Ritonavir increases macitentan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Ritonavir increases maraviroc levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Decrease the maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 45. Marijuana increases ritonavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, and ritonavir increases marijuana levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Ritonavir increases mavacamten levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure from systolic dysfunction. 47. Mavorixafor increases ritonavir levels by altering CYP2D6 metabolism and inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 48. Ritonavir increases medroxyprogesterone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 49. Ritonavir increases mefloquine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing toxicity risk. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Ritonavir increases meperidine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
